units.text: The interval from Constitution signing (1787) to Bill of Rights ratification (1791) is 4 years, while the interval from congressional proposal (September 1789) to ratification (December 1791) is approximately 2 years and 3 months. The first interval exceeds the second.

citations.title: The Bill of Rights: A Transcription | National Archives

judgement.reason: The passages support the proposal and ratification dates, making the second interval about 2 years and 3 months and showing the first interval is longer. However, from September 17, 1787 to December 15, 1791 is more than 4 years (about 4 years and 3 months), so the statement that the first interval is 4 years is not exactly supported.

units.text: Constitution signing occurred September 17, 1787 in Philadelphia (span 21). Congressional proposal of 12 amendments occurred September 25, 1789 (span 29 and 12). Bill of Rights ratified December 15, 1791 (span 33 and 14).

citations.title: The Bill of Rights: A Transcription | National Archives

judgement.reason: The passages state the Constitution was signed September 17, 1787 in Philadelphia; 12 amendments were proposed/approved by Congress on September 25, 1789; and the Bill of Rights amendments were ratified on December 15, 1791.

units.text: Madison proposed 19 amendments on June 8, 1789; 12 were approved September 25, 1789; 10 became the Bill of Rights upon ratification December 15, 1791 (spans 29, 31, 33).

citations.title: The Bill of Rights: A Transcription | National Archives

judgement.reason: Passages confirm Madison proposed 19 amendments on June 8, 1789, 12 were approved September 25, 1789, and 10 were ratified December 15, 1791, but they do not mention the parenthetical '(spans 29, 31, 33)'.
